title: Petronet LNG Ltd - 532522 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.
summary.overview: Standalone PBT rose 33% YoY to INR 1,514 crore and PAT to INR 1,133 crore, with consolidated PBT of INR 1,491 crore described as the highest ever Q1. Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.

segments.name: Dahej terminal
segments.commentary: Processed 192 TBTU in Q1 FY27 versus 207 TBTU a year ago and 201 TBTU in Q4; utilisation 66% on 22.5 MMTPA expanded capacity (65.6% per call) versus 92% a year ago.

segments.name: Kochi terminal
segments.commentary: Utilisation 23.27% in Q1 FY27 as stated on the call; pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of the quarter.

segments.name: Company overall
segments.commentary: Processed 207 TBTU (vs 220 TBTU YoY, 219 TBTU QoQ); utilisation 58% vs 76% in both prior periods.

guidance_outlook: Capex budgeted at INR 9,064 crore for FY27, with similar levels expected for FY28.
Utilisation expected to improve slightly: April was low, May and June ran at the rate that continues into the quarter, and recovery depends on reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Contract talks with offtakers on tariffs or renewal expected to close in the next 2 to 3 quarters; no tariff revision discussion currently.
New Qatar contract to start in 2028; it will be on DES basis, with a formula-driven price that includes shipping.
Petchem project is on schedule, about 40% complete on physical progress; propane contract signing expected in 2027.
capex_capacity: Dahej nameplate capacity increased from 17.5 MMTPA to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026; Dahej utilisation 66% on the expanded base.
Kochi utilisation 23.27% in Q1; Kochi pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of Q1 FY27 (end-June quarter per management).
Petchem project about 40% complete physically; capex INR 472 crore in the quarter, cumulative INR 679 crore.
FY27 capex budget INR 9,064 crore; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Petchem: 600 KTPA ethane handling contract and a Deepak Phenolics contract signed; equity IRR not disclosed for now as commercial contracts are still being finalised.
demand_pricing: Term volumes fell sharply; third-party regas and tolling volumes filled the gap, and management said more than two-thirds of the missing Middle East volume is being replaced by these customers.
Qatar force majeure is declared month by month, and was declared for end-August at the time of the call; offtakers are booking volumes on a month-to-month basis.
Spot trading was small (about 6 TBTU in the quarter per management), yet produced material trading gains when spot prices were well above long-term prices.
Deepak Fertilizers contract (about 0.5 MTPA expected at Dahej) began May 2026 with 2 cargoes brought so far; ExxonMobil volume increase at Kochi also started.
Tariffs at Dahej around INR 69 and at Kochi around INR 98 for the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has the term-versus-third-party volume mix persisted into Q2, and should it hold until the Gulf conflict resolves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pattern continued into Q2 so far; it hopes Qatar volumes resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the margin improvement come from; is there an inventory gain and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading gains INR 301 crore and inventory gains INR 193 crore; management described trading gains during spot-price spikes as the established business model over the past 5-6 years, without committing to a Q2 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation by terminal and the FY27/FY28 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej 65.6%, Kochi 23.27%; recovery depends on Hormuz reopening, and May-June run-rate is slightly better than April.

qa_highlights.question: Use-or-pay treatment of tolling cargoes?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling cargoes from non-GAIL offtakers can offset use-or-pay after current-year commitments are met; GAIL has no use-or-pay, and the long-term take-or-pay contract is separate.

qa_highlights.question: Ind AS impacts for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin impact positive INR 14 crore, forex loss INR 5 crore, other expenses positive INR 8 crore, depreciation INR 66 crore, finance cost INR 48 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are time-charter vessel costs being paid during force majeure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said time-charter vessel operations have been suspended under clauses other than force majeure, so charter costs are not being paid.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz closure and Qatar supply: no timing given; FM declared month-to-month.
Dependence on spot-price spreads for trading and inventory gains, which management did not say would persist into Q2.
Utilisation at Dahej (66%) and company level (58%) against the enlarged capacity base.
Tariff renewal with offtakers, expected in 2 to 3 quarters.
Petchem project economics: IRR not disclosed; commercial contracts still pending.
Ongoing time-charter cost treatment and the contracted vessel fleet after DES shift.
summary.management_tone: ["Confident on earnings resilience and the trading business model, with the Q1 PAT and PBT growth framed as a strong start.","Cautious and non-committal on volumes: Hormuz timing is unknown, and management repeatedly said recovery depends on geopolitics. Evasive on petchem IRR and the Q2 margin outlook."]
key_quotes: Overall, I would say it has been a strong start to the year, while volumes were somewhat lower, we have delivered a healthy financial performance supported by commercial and operational efficiencies.
Inventory gains are at INR193 crores and trading gains are at INR301 crores.

financial_highlights.value: INR 472 crore (about INR 470 crore stated in same answer)
financial_highlights.change: Cumulative petchem capex to date INR 679 crore per management

adds.what: Dahej nameplate capacity raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA (done 31 Mar 2026)
Kochi pipeline connectivity (mechanically complete expected end of Q1 FY27)

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; volumes fell (company utilisation 58% vs 76%, Qatar force majeure) with recovery tied to Strait of Hormuz reopening, partly offset by third-party tolling/regas volumes replacing two-thirds of the missing Middle East volume, and a Petchem build-out about 40% complete with FY27 capex budget of INR 9,064 crore.
